errors.text: The hypothesis says dislocation density peaks or remains high at 600 K, whereas the target reports reduced dislocation density at 600 K, associated with the elastic-modulus increase.

It elevates localized amorphization and an FCC-to-HCP-like phase collapse to the primary mechanism without direct evidence; HCP-classified atoms in FCC metals can instead represent stacking faults or partial-dislocation activity.

The proposed 'HCP-stabilized' simulation is not a clean or physically defined control: stabilizing HCP atoms could promote rather than prevent transformation and would alter the interatomic energy landscape, confounding friction and defect evolution.
